newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan court reinstates ousted chief minister.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan court reinstates ousted chief minister.

text.p: A Pakistani court reinstated the ousted chief minister of Punjab province on Sunday in a setback to Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto.
The Lahore High Court gave Manzoor Wattoo, who was ousted in September 1995 on Bhutto's recommendation, 10 days to prove his majority in the assembly in Pakistan's most populous province.

The three-member bench said in its order that if Wattoo failed to win a vote of confidence, outgoing chief minister Arif Nakai, whose party is in Bhutto's federal governing coalition, would be returned to power in Punjab.

President Farooq Leghari, acting on Bhutto's mandatory advice, suspended Wattoo last year after a revolt by most provincial ministers. Nakai later assumed power in the eastern province that borders India.
Newspapers had said Wattoo's reinstatement would be a blow to Bhutto's government, which has been under pressure from opposition protests.
The Lahore court ordered Wattoo, whose faction of the Pakistan Muslim League has only a handful of members in the Punjab provincial assembly, not to dissolve the legislature.
